input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# Platform Operator midstream repository onboarding

## Description

Establish the midstream repository for the Platform Operator component under the opendatahub-io organization. The Platform Operator is listed as an affected component of the FIPS 140-3 compliance strategy, but the platform's architecture-context inventory has no file for it, so it is treated as a component not yet in the platform and provisioned through the standard onboarding chain. This epic provides the repository foundation that the Platform Operator's build-pipeline onboarding and FIPS remediation work build on.

## Scope

- Confirm the upstream source project for the Platform Operator and check whether a midstream repository already exists (the platform inventory records none; if one is discovered, this epic reduces to recording and validating it).
- Create the midstream repository fork under opendatahub-io, following the conventions used by the platform's other midstream repositories.
- Establish the default branch, branch protection, and basic change workflow so downstream build and remediation work can proceed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A midstream Platform Operator repository exists under opendatahub-io (or a pre-existing one is identified and validated), mirroring the upstream source at a recorded state.
- The repository follows the standard opendatahub-io midstream conventions applied to peer components.
- The repository state (new vs. pre-existing) and the pinned upstream source are recorded for the downstream build-pipeline onboarding.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (enabling): provides the midstream repository foundation required to remediate the Platform Operator's serving-stack images for FIPS-enabled clusters.

# Platform Operator license validation

## Description

Validate the licenses of the Platform Operator component's transitive dependency tree ahead of its FIPS remediation. License problems discovered after implementation starts would force dependency changes that alter the remediation approach, so the scan runs up front, in parallel with repository onboarding.

## Scope

- Scan the Platform Operator's dependency tree (direct and transitive) for license obligations and restrictions.
- Produce a license-validation verdict listing any dependency whose license blocks or constrains use in the platform's container images.
- For each problematic dependency, identify the remediation path (exclude, replace, or document the obligation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Platform Operator's transitive dependency tree has been scanned and the results recorded.
- Every license issue found is documented with a concrete remediation path.
- The license verdict is available to the Platform Operator FIPS remediation work before it builds against the dependency set.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (enabling): ensures the dependency set the FIPS remediation builds against is license-clear, so remediation is not reworked mid-flight.

# Platform Operator Konflux build pipeline onboarding

## Description

Onboard the Platform Operator's midstream repository to the Konflux build pipeline so the component's images are built through the platform's standard pipeline, with the provenance and attestation capabilities the compliance evidence package consumes. This work starts once the midstream repository exists.

## Scope

- Konflux onboarding configuration for the Platform Operator repository (application and component definitions, build recipe), following the standard onboarding recipe.
- First complete build of the component's images through the pipeline.
- Confirmation that the pipeline produces build attestations for the built images, in the form the compliance evidence package consumes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Platform Operator repository is onboarded to Konflux following the standard onboarding recipe.
- The pipeline produces a green build of the Platform Operator images.
- Signed build attestations are produced by the pipeline for the built images and are retrievable for the compliance evidence package.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (enabling): the pipeline builds the images the FIPS remediation changes.
- HLR-2 (enabling): the pipeline produces the build attestations the compliance evidence package includes.

# KServe FIPS crypto remediation for serving-stack images

## Description

Remove non-validated cryptographic library usage from KServe's serving-stack images so they run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated crypto modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request path. KServe's midstream repositories and Konflux build pipeline already exist, so this work starts immediately.

## Scope

- Build a complete module inventory of non-validated crypto usage across the KServe serving-stack images (KServe components and the serving data plane).
- Remediate the identified usage: replace or rebuild the linked crypto libraries with validated modules, adjusting base images and build configuration as needed.
- Verify the remediated images on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters across the serving request path (deployment and inference serving).
- Confirm serving behavior is unchanged on non-FIPS clusters.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A module inventory documents every non-validated crypto usage found in the KServe serving-stack images and the remediation applied to each.
- All KServe serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, with no non-validated crypto in the request path, verified by tests executed on a FIPS-enabled cluster.
- Serving behavior on non-FIPS clusters is unchanged (regression verification).
- The existing Konflux build pipeline builds the remediated KServe images green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (primary): KServe share of "all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path)".

# Platform Operator FIPS crypto remediation

## Description

Remove non-validated cryptographic library usage from the Platform Operator's images so the operator runs correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated crypto modules. This work starts once the component's midstream repository exists and its dependency licenses have been validated; it proceeds in parallel with the component's build-pipeline onboarding, with the pipeline coupling enforced by a "build pipeline green" acceptance criterion rather than a scheduling dependency.

## Scope

- Extend the crypto module inventory to the Platform Operator's images, identifying all non-validated crypto usage.
- Remediate the identified usage by replacing or rebuilding linked crypto libraries with validated modules.
- Verify the remediated operator on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters (deployment and management of the serving stack).
- Confirm operator behavior is unchanged on non-FIPS clusters.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The module inventory covers the Platform Operator images, documenting each non-validated crypto usage and its remediation.
- The remediated Platform Operator runs correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, with no non-validated crypto in the request path, verified by tests executed on a FIPS-enabled cluster.
- Operator behavior on non-FIPS clusters is unchanged (regression verification).
- The component's Konflux build pipeline builds the remediated images green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (primary): Platform Operator share of "all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path)".

# CI gating check for FIPS crypto regressions in serving-stack builds

## Description

A gating CI check that fails any serving-stack build which reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, so the FIPS-remediated state of the model serving stack cannot regress unnoticed. The check is developed independently of the remediation work and runs gating in the serving-stack build pipelines, including the Platform Operator pipeline once that component is onboarded.

## Scope

- Implement the regression check: detection of non-validated crypto usage in the images produced by serving-stack builds.
- Wire the check as a gating step in the serving-stack build pipelines (Konflux), covering KServe builds and the Platform Operator builds.
- Define the check's failure output so an offending build identifies the non-validated usage it introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage fails the gating check, with output identifying the offending usage.
- The check runs as a gating step in the serving-stack build pipelines, covering both KServe and Platform Operator builds.
- The check passes on the FIPS-remediated serving-stack images (no false positives on the remediated state).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (primary): "CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage."

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and submission

## Description

Assemble the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving stack — the crypto module inventory, build attestations, and test results — and submit it through the security review board to the external accredited certification laboratory. The package is assembled once the serving-stack remediation work has produced its outcomes; the build attestations are consumed as content from the serving-stack Konflux build pipelines.

## Scope

- Compile the module inventory of cryptographic modules across the serving-stack images from the remediation outcomes (KServe and Platform Operator).
- Collect the signed build attestations produced by the serving-stack Konflux build pipelines, including the Platform Operator pipeline.
- Collect the FIPS-enabled-cluster test results produced by the remediation work.
- Assemble the package in the form the security review board and certification laboratory require, and submit it through the review board to the lab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains the complete module inventory, the signed build attestations from the serving-stack build pipelines, and the FIPS-enabled-cluster test results for the remediated images.
- The evidence package is submitted through the security review board to the external certification laboratory.

## Risks / Notes

- Certification-laboratory turnaround is historically six to nine months, and security-review-board sign-off occurs at defined milestones. Both are externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort; they dominate the delivery schedule for certified compliance (strategy problem statement and open-questions note). The engineering deliverable this epic controls is the assembled, submitted package — the certification outcome arrives on the laboratory's schedule.
- Once submitted, the certification laboratory triages the package at intake on its own schedule. Intake triage and the certification verdict are externally controlled outcomes, not deliverables of this epic; this epic's deliverable ends at a complete package submitted through the security review board.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (primary): "A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab."

Document the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, reflecting the implemented and validated state of the stack. This work starts once all serving-stack implementation work in the strategy has landed, so the documentation describes what was built.

## Scope

- FIPS support posture of the model serving stack: what is supported, on which serving-stack images, and the validated crypto-module basis.
- Cluster prerequisites: FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster requirements and any configuration prerequisites resulting from the remediation.
- Operational guidance for running the serving stack on FIPS-enabled clusters, covering the deployment modes the serving stack supports.
- Statements kept consistent with the compliance evidence package and the CI enforcement behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented serving stack, with review sign-off recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (primary): "Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites."
